question.title: Guilford County Local Sales And Use Tax Referendum

threshold.rule: Every county sales and use tax referendum provision in G.S. Chapter 105 in force 2008-2026 (Art. 46 quarter-cent, Art. 43 transportation, Art. 39 one-cent) uses the same test: the majority of those voting in the referendum must vote for the levy. The title does not say which Article a given question was held under, so the Art. 46 sentence (the one that fits the quarter-cent referendums of 2008-2026) is the main quote and the others are in also_cited. Inferred, not stated, for this reason.
threshold.quote: If the majority of those voting in a referendum held pursuant to this Article vote for the levy of the tax, the board of county commissioners may, by resolution and after 10 days' public notice, levy a local sales and use tax at a rate of one-quarter percent (0.25%).
threshold.matched: by the kind the source's words show (county local sales and use tax referendum (article not named in title)); every county sales and use tax article that puts the levy to the voters (39, 43, 46) sets this share; the title does not name the article

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures

question.title: Guilford County School Bonds Referendum

threshold.rule: The bond order takes effect on the affirmative vote of a majority of those who vote on the question (the constitution: 'a majority of the qualified voters of the unit who vote thereon'). The title does not say 'general obligation', but the Local Government Bond Act (G.S. 159-49) puts every bond that needs a vote under this test; revenue bonds need no vote. Section 159-61 is headed 'Bond referenda; majority required', so the kind is named by the law; the only reading made is that each title containing 'bond' is such a referendum.
threshold.quote: If a bond order is to take effect upon approval of the voters, the affirmative vote or a majority of those who vote thereon shall be required.
threshold.matched: by the kind the source's words show (general obligation bond referendum: school, community college or county library bonds); a school, community college or library is not among the services a county service district may provide (G.S. 153A-301, read), so G.S. 153A-308's concurrent majorities cannot apply [inferred from the title]

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures

question.title: Town Of Spring Hope Mixed Beverage Election

threshold.rule: G.S. 18B-602(h) sets only the ballot words for a mixed beverage election; the result rule is not in that subsection. G.S. 18B-601(a) runs an alcoholic beverage election 'in the same manner and under the same rules as a referendum under Chapter 163'; G.S. 18B-604(b) speaks of 'a majority of voters' voting in favor of alcoholic beverage sales; G.S. 163-182.15(d) says that in a referendum the proposal with the highest number of votes prevails. Read together: more FOR than AGAINST (a simple majority of those voting on the question). Inferred because no sentence of Article 6 states the threshold for mixed beverage elections by name.
threshold.quote: If a majority of voters vote in favor of certain alcoholic beverage sales in a county election, sale of that kind of alcoholic beverage shall be lawful throughout the county

question.title: ALAMANCE COUNTY LOCAL SALES AND USE TAX

forecasts.fitted_on: North Carolina's State Board local questions of 2008-2019

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures

threshold.rule: Every county sales and use tax referendum provision in G.S. Chapter 105 in force 2008-2026 (Art. 46 quarter-cent, Art. 43 transportation, Art. 39 one-cent) uses the same test: the majority of those voting in the referendum must vote for the levy. The title does not say which Article a given question was held under, so the Art. 46 sentence (the one that fits the quarter-cent referendums of 2008-2026) is the main quote and the others are in also_cited. Inferred, not stated, for this reason.
threshold.quote: If the majority of those voting in a referendum held pursuant to this Article vote for the levy of the tax, the board of county commissioners may, by resolution and after 10 days' public notice, levy a local sales and use tax at a rate of one-quarter percent (0.25%).

question.title: ROWAN COUNTY COMMUNITY COLLEGE BONDS

forecasts.fitted_on: North Carolina's State Board local questions of 2008-2019

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures

threshold.rule: The bond order takes effect on the affirmative vote of a majority of those who vote on the question (the constitution: 'a majority of the qualified voters of the unit who vote thereon'). The title does not say 'general obligation', but the Local Government Bond Act (G.S. 159-49) puts every bond that needs a vote under this test; revenue bonds need no vote. Section 159-61 is headed 'Bond referenda; majority required', so the kind is named by the law; the only reading made is that each title containing 'bond' is such a referendum.
threshold.quote: If a bond order is to take effect upon approval of the voters, the affirmative vote or a majority of those who vote thereon shall be required.
threshold.matched: by the kind the source's words show (general obligation bond referendum: school, community college or county library bonds); a school, community college or library is not among the services a county service district may provide (G.S. 153A-301, read), so G.S. 153A-308's concurrent majorities cannot apply [inferred from the title]

contests.election: election on 2020-03-03, not a November general (the source does not say its kind)

question.title: DAVIE COUNTY MALT BEVERAGE ELECTION - HOTELS, ETC.

forecasts.fitted_on: North Carolina's State Board local questions of 2008-2019

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures

threshold.rule: The kind of malt beverage sales on a proposition is allowed if that proposition receives a majority of the votes FOR (each voter votes on each proposition; FOR versus AGAINST). Township elections are decided 'in the same manner as county elections' (G.S. 18B-600(f)). Titles with 'Hotels, Etc.', 'Off Premises', 'On Premises' etc. are separate propositions under § 18B-602(a), each with the same test.
threshold.quote: The kind of malt beverage sales described in each proposition that receives a majority of votes "FOR" shall be allowed.
